title: element:button's forward payload is cast `as any`, so it absorbs invented keys — the third unchecked forward literal
body:
Found while implementing #4281 (the two action-renderer sites). Filed rather than fixed: out of that card's scope, and its fix is a different change.

## What

#4281 fixed the two *action* renderers whose `execute({ … })` payload was not excess-property checked. `check:action-forward-parity` now asserts that property structurally for every surface it knows. A fifth surface, `element:button`, fails the same assertion for a **different reason**, and ships with a declared `UNCHECKED_FORWARDS` exemption pointing here.

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx` — the `execute(...)` argument at `:231` is an `AsExpression` whose type is `any`:

```ts
await execute({
  type: action.actionType || action.type,
  name: action.name,
  ...
  refreshAfter: action.refreshAfter,
  ...paramsPayload,
} as any);
```

Measured on TypeScript 6.0.3: `{ … } as any` switches the excess-property check off completely — an assertion asks only for comparability. So every one of the ~16 keys in that literal rides unchecked, exactly as #4281's two sites did before their fix, and `ActionDef` being closed (#4046) buys this surface nothing.

## Why it is not simply the same fix

The four action renderers take a typed action (`ActionSchema`) and their `localContext` spread was the accidental cause. Here the cast looks deliberate: `props.action` is declared `action?: Record< string, any >`, so the renderer never had a typed action to begin with. Removing the cast is therefore a **contract** change (what does `element:button` accept?), not the mechanical hoist #4281 applied — which is why #4281 exempted it rather than guessing.

Every key the literal currently writes (`type`, `name`, `label`, `description`, `target`, `openIn`, `endpoint`, `method`, `navigate`, `to`, `opensInNewTab`, `bodyExtra`, `confirmText`, `successMessage`, `errorMessage`, `refreshAfter`, plus `params`/`actionParams` via the spread) IS declared on `ActionDef`, so dropping the cast may well compile as-is — but that wants measuring, not assuming, and the `Record< string, any >` prop type is the real question underneath.

## Where the exemption lives

`scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` → `UNCHECKED_FORWARDS['element:button']`. It is **ratcheted**: once the payload becomes checked, the entry itself fails the gate and must be deleted. So this cannot rot silently.

## Not a live user-visible defect today

Nothing is currently mis-forwarded here — `check:action-forward-parity`'s parity half is green for this surface on the inline contract. The cost is the missing compile-time guarantee: a typo added to this list tomorrow would be silent.

Refs #4281, #4046, #4050.
